title: Caring for Others Don't Forget Yourself, Says Study
paragraphs: Caring for a family member who is sick, elderly or disabled can be extremely rewarding, but it can also be exhausting. Experts are now reminding caregivers that looking after themselves is not a luxury, but a necessity.

The number of caregivers in the United States has grown dramatically. According to a report by the National Alliance for Caregiving and AARP, nearly one in four American adults, or about 63 million people, provided care to adults or children with medical conditions or disabilities in 2025. That figure has risen by almost 50% over the past decade. The report also found that caregiving, which is mostly unpaid, has become longer and more intense, and nearly two-thirds of caregivers reported high levels of emotional stress.

Because caregivers are so focused on the needs of others, they often neglect their own health and well-being. This can eventually lead to burnout. Jessica Renda, who leads a support group for parents and caregivers with the New Hampshire chapter of the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI), put it simply: you cannot be a good caregiver to somebody else if you are not taking care of yourself. Experts emphasize that self-care looks different for each person, and it does not have to be expensive or time-consuming. As Renda pointed out, self-care does not have to mean a day at the spa. Even a few quiet minutes, such as sitting in a parked car after work, can make a difference.

Susan Stearns, the executive director of NAMI New Hampshire, offers several practical suggestions. Caregivers can ask a neighbor or relative to cover for them so they can take a short break. They should also prioritize sleep and physical activity, even if it is just a brief walk. Staying connected with others, whether in person, by phone or through online support groups, is also important. Finally, Stearns says it is fine to say no and to let go of unrealistic expectations.
Jennifer Rabalais of the University of New Hampshire points out that many people do not even realize they are caregivers.
